Chocolate collections in these sets are inspired by the exquisite perfume compositions of the twentieth century and dedicated to a talented young perfumer lady, who gifted the world with these remarkable fragrances.   The miniature perfume bottles are crafted using familiar bonbons molds. The compositions adorning the chocolate bars are hand-painted with cocoa butter directly on the mold, as well as on delicate sheets of acetate film carefully placed on top of the chocolate bars. Thanks to this meticulous approach, each piece in the collection is imbued with a special mood, as if it preserves within itself fragrant stories from the last century. . . Шоколадные коллекции данных наборов , вдохновлены изысканными парфюмерными композициями XX века и посвещены талантливой девушке-парфюмеру, подарившей миру эти удивительные ароматы.   Миниатюрные флакончики для духов реализованны с помощью привычных форм для конфет. I just wanted to bake chocolate lava cakes... Instead Evelyn cracked me, in more way than one. 🥀🍫😭 #househusbandbakes #evelynchevalier #evelynzzz #animecouplegoals #animetok  This recipe makes 4 chocolate lava cakes.  Ingredients:  • 1/2 cup (4 ounces) unsalted butter, plus more for greasing the ramekins • 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting the ramekins • 6 ounces bittersweet or dark chocolate, chopped (about 1 cup plus 1 1/2 tablespoons) You can sub in chocolate chips if its all you have. • 2 large eggs, room temperature • 2 large egg yolks, room temperature • 1/4 cup granulated sugar • 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt Directions:  Gather the ingredients. ● Preheat oven to 450°F. Butter and lightly flour four 6-ounce ramekins. Tap out excess flour. Set the ramekins on a baking sheet. ● Fill a pan/pot with water to a depth of 1 or 2 Inches depending on the depth of the pot; bring to a boil over medium-high and reduce heat to medium-low to maintain a simmer. Combine chocolate and butter in a medium size heatproof bowl and set bowl over simmering water in pan, making sure bottom of bowl doesn't touch water. Cook over medium-low, stirring occasionally and adjusting heat as needed to maintain a simmer, until chocolate mixture is melted and smooth, 10 to 20 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside. ● Beat eggs, egg yolks, sugar, and salt in a medium bowl with an electric mixer fitted with the whisk attachment on high speed until thickened and pale, 2 to 3 minutes ● Whisk melted chocolate until smooth ● Quickly fold melted chocolate mixture and flour into egg mixture in bowl until well combined and no streaks remain. ● Spoon batter into prepared ramekins (about 1/2 cup per ramekin) and smooth the top using a small offset spatula if needed. Place baking sheet with ramekins in the preheated oven; bake until tops of cakes are just set and edges spring back when touched but centers still feel soft, about 9 to 12 minutes. ● Remove cakes from oven and let cool in ramekins on baking sheet for 1 minute. Working with one ramekin at a time, cover ramekin with an inverted plate. Carefully turn over and let stand 10 seconds before lifting the ramekin to unmold cake. Repeat with remaining cakes. Dust with powdered sugar if you want the dominos pizza lavs cake look. Serve immediately or refrigerate for up to 3 days. Microwave briefly to reheat.

The Hershey Chocolate Explanation: Most people know the chocolate. Few know the struggle behind Milton S. Hershey. Before success, he failed repeatedly. In the late 1800s, his candy businesses in Philadelphia, Chicago, and New York all collapsed. He returned home broke, with bad credit and a reputation as a failure. But he didn’t stop. In 1886, he built the Lancaster Caramel Company using fresh milk, and it became a global success. Then came his biggest risk. After seeing chocolate machinery in 1893, he sold his entire caramel business in 1900 and bet everything on milk chocolate. It worked. He built a factory, a town, and a brand that changed the industry forever. His story proves one thing — failure isn’t the end. It’s often the beginning.
